en: Free from error; true; accurate.
With good manners; well behaved; conforming with accepted standards of behaviour.
Correctly.
Used to indicate acknowledgement or acceptance.
A correct response.

correct.ety: Borrowed from French correct, from Latin correctus (“improved, amended, correct”), past participle of corrigere, conrigere (“to make straight, make right, make better, improve, correct”), from con- (“together”) + combining form of regō, regere (“I rule, make straight”).

ex.en: Your answer to the question is not correct.
ex.ja: その問題に対するあなたの解答は正確ではない。

ex.en: You would do well to correct your mistakes.
ex.ja: 誤りを訂正するほうが賢明であろう。

ex.en: The sign means that the answer is correct.
ex.ja: その記号は答えが正しいことを示す。

note.ja: cor（完全に）+ rect（まっすぐ）。完全にまっすぐな →「正しい・訂正する」。direct（まっすぐな）、rectangle（直角の四角形）も同じ rect。

en: Full of danger.
Causing danger; ready to do harm or injury.

dangerous.ety:
From Middle English daungerous (“difficult, severe, domineering, arrogant, fraught with danger”), dangerous, from Anglo-Norman [Term?], from Old French dangereus (“threatening, difficult”), from dangier. Equivalent to danger + -ous.
Displaced native Old English frēcne.

ex.en: It's dangerous to go out alone after dark.
ex.ja: 暗くなってから一人で出歩くのは危ないよ。

ex.en: It is dangerous to cross that old bridge.
ex.ja: そのふるい橋をわたるのは危ない。

ex.en: I think it dangerous walking alone at night.
ex.ja: 夜道を１人で歩くのは危険だと思います。

note.ja: danger（危険）+ -ous。danger はラテン語 dominium（支配）から。「支配される力」→「危険」。dominate と同系。

en: To an extreme degree.

extremely.ety:
Etymology tree
English extreme
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English extremely
From extreme + -ly.

ex.en: I was extremely surprised when I saw this.
ex.ja: これを見たときはびっくり仰天した。

ex.en: She is extremely natural in her manner.
ex.ja: 彼女の態度は極めて自然である。

ex.en: That person is extremely annoying, aren't they.
ex.ja: 迷惑極まりない人ね。

note.ja: extreme（極端な）+ -ly。ラテン語 extremus（最も外側の）。exterior と同じ。

en: A business partnership; the name under which it trades.
A business enterprise, however organized.
Steadfast, secure, solid (in position)
Fixed (in opinion).
To make firm or strong; fix securely.
To make compact or resistant to pressure; solidify.

firm.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin firmoder.
Italian firmarebf.
Italian firmabor.
English firm
From Italian firma (“signature”), from firmare (“to sign”), from Latin firmāre (“to make firm, to confirm (by signature)”), from firmus (“firm, stable”). The contemporary sense developed in the 18th century simultaneously with German Firma (“business, name of business”). There are conflicting statements in the literature as to which of the two languages influenced which. Doublet of dharma and dhamma. Other cognates include Russian держать (deržatʹ, “to hold”).

ex.en: There are many commercial firms in New York.
ex.ja: ニューヨークにはたくさんの商社がある。

ex.en: He stood firm in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても動じなかった。

ex.en: I got a temporary job at the firm.
ex.ja: 私はその会社で臨時の仕事を得た。

note.ja: 「しっかりした」はラテン語 firmus（固い）から。「会社」は同じ語からで、署名（firma）で事業を確定することから。confirm と同じ。

en: The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.
An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.
To touch; to feel or hold with the hand(s).
To manage, use, or wield with the hands.

handle.ety: From Middle English handel, handle, from Old English handle (“handle”), from Proto-West Germanic *handulā (“handle”). See verb below. Cognate with German Hantel (“dumbbell, barbell”), Danish handel (“handle”). Related to hand.

ex.en: Do you think you can handle this problem?
ex.ja: この問題が自分の手に負えると思ってる？

ex.en: I put a new handle to the door.
ex.ja: 私は戸に新しい取っ手を付けた。

ex.en: Do you think that you can handle it?
ex.ja: 自分の手に負えると思う？

note.ja: hand（手）+ -le（道具）。「手でつかむところ」→「取っ手」→「扱う」。車のハンドルは英語では steering wheel。

en: To make (something) better; to increase the value or productivity (of something).
To become better.

improve.ety: From Anglo-Norman emprouwer, from Old French en- + prou (“profit”), from Vulgar Latin prode (“advantageous, profitable”).

ex.en: I think your English has improved a lot.
ex.ja: 君の英語はとても上達したと思う。

ex.en: With the approach of Christmas, business improved somewhat.
ex.ja: クリスマスが近づくにつれて景気はいくらか回復した。

ex.en: I’d like to improve my guitar skills.
ex.ja: ギターもっと上手くなりたいな。

note.ja: 古フランス語 en prou（利益に）から。「利益にする」→「改善する」。prove とは別語源。

en: Synonym of actually or truly.
In fact.
Indicates agreement with another speaker's previous statement.
Indicates doubt or disagreement with another speaker's previous statement.

indeed.ety: From Middle English indede, univerbation of the phrase in dede (“in sooth, in fact”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian innerdoat, innedoat (“indeed”), West Frisian yndied (“indeed”), Dutch inderdaad (“indeed”), German in der Tat (“indeed”). By surface analysis, in + deed. Compare in fact, in truth, etc. First attested in the early 14ᵗʰ century.

ex.en: Very funny! You are indeed a funny person.
ex.ja: おかしすぎる！あなたって、面白い人ね。

ex.en: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
ex.ja: まさかの時の友は真の友。

ex.en: I am indeed very glad to hear that.
ex.ja: それを聞いて全くうれしい。

note.ja: in + deed（行為・事実）。「事実として」→「実に・本当に」。

en: Not positive or neutral; bad; undesirable; unfavourable.
Of a number: less than zero.
Refusal or withholding of assents; prohibition, veto
An unfavorable point or characteristic.
To refuse; to veto.
To contradict.
No; nay.

negative.ety: From Middle English negative, negatif, from Old French negatif, from Latin negātīvus (“that denies, negative”), from negāre (“to deny”); see negate.

ex.en: Well you know, negative form translation is difficult!
ex.ja: 否定形ってさぁ、訳すの難しんだよ。

ex.en: Some people argue that technology has negative effects.
ex.ja: 科学技術にはマイナスの影響があると主張する者もいる。

ex.en: I don't like a negative sort of man.
ex.ja: 消極的な男は嫌いだ。

note.ja: neg（否定する）+ ative。否定する →「否定的な・負の・陰性の」。neglect（拾わない→無視する）、deny（否定する）も同じ。

en: To stop (an outcome); to keep from (doing something).

prevent.ety: From Middle English preventen (“anticipate”), from Latin praeventus, perfect passive participle of praeveniō (“to anticipate”), from prae (“before”) + veniō (“to come”).

ex.en: There is nothing to prevent us from going.
ex.ja: 私たちが行くのを妨げるものは何もない。

ex.en: We took strong measures to prevent it.
ex.ja: 私たちはそれを防止する強硬な対策を講じた。

ex.en: The real issue is how to prevent the disease.
ex.ja: 本当の問題はどうやってその病気を予防するかである。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ vent（来る）。先回りして来る →（行く手をふさぐ）→「妨げる・防ぐ」。

en: To delete.
To move from one place to another, especially to take away.
The act of removing something.
A dish served to replace an earlier one during a meal; a part of a new course.

remove.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-
Proto-Indo-European *m(y)ewh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *-éyeti
Proto-Indo-European *m(y)owh₁éyeti
Proto-Italic *moweō
Latin moveō
Latin removeō
Old French removoir
Anglo-Norman removerbor.
Middle English removen
English remove
From Middle English removen, from Anglo-Norman remover, removeir, from Old French remouvoir, from Latin removēre, from re- + movēre (“to move”), equivalent to re- + move. Displaced native Old English āfierran.

ex.en: Your name has been removed from the list.
ex.ja: あなたはリストから外されたよ。

ex.en: Please remove your shoes before entering the house.
ex.ja: 靴を脱いでから家には入ってください。

ex.en: I removed the English and Japanese language links.
ex.ja: 英語と日本語のリンクを外しました。

note.ja: re（離して）+ movere（動かす）。「動かして離す」→「取り除く」。move と同じ。

en: The soul of a person or other creature.
A supernatural being, often but not exclusively without physical form; ghost, fairy, angel.
To carry off, especially in haste, secrecy, or mystery.
Sometimes followed by up: to animate with vigour; to excite; to encourage; to inspirit.

spirit.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)peys-der.?
Latin spīrō

Proto-Italic *-tus

Latin spīrituslbor.

Middle English spirit
English spirit
From Middle English spirit, from Old French espirit (“spirit”), from Latin spīritus (“breath; spirit”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)peys- (“to blow, breathe”). Compare inspire, respire, transpire, all ultimately from Latin spīrō (“to breathe, blow, respire”). In this sense, displaced native Middle English gast (from Old English gāst), whence modern English ghost. Doublet of spiritus, spirytus, spri

ex.en: They may be poor, but rich in spirit.
ex.ja: 彼らは貧しいかもしれないが、心は豊かだ。

ex.en: He entered into the game with great spirit.
ex.ja: 彼は元気に試合に参加した。

ex.en: So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
ex.ja: 御霊によって生まれるものも、皆そのとおりです。

note.ja: ラテン語 spiritus（息）から。spir（息をする）。息 →「精神・霊・気力」。inspire（息を吹き込む→着想を与える）、respiration（呼吸）も同じ。

en: An electronic communication medium that allows the transmission of real-time visual images, and often sound.
An electronic home entertainment device equipped with a screen and a speaker for receiving television signals and displaying them in audi…
To watch television.

television.ety:
Etymology tree

From tele- + vision. First attested in 1900, probably influenced by French télévision from Constantin Perskyi's 1900 paper that was unpublished but presented at a Paris conference.

ex.en: Instead of watching television, the children played outside.
ex.ja: 子供たちはテレビを見ないで外で遊んだ。

ex.en: What sort of television programs are on today?
ex.ja: 今日はどんなテレビ番組がありますか。

ex.en: She has been watching television for three hours.
ex.ja: 彼女は３時間テレビを見続けている。

note.ja: tele（遠く）+ vis（見る）+ ion。遠くのものを見ること →「テレビ」。telephone（遠くの音）、telescope（遠くを見る道具）と同じ tele。

en: Until; to, up to; as late as (a given time).
Before (a certain time or event).
Until, until the time that.
A cash register.
A removable box within a cash register containing the money.
To develop so as to improve or prepare for usage; to cultivate (said of knowledge, virtue, mind etc.).
To work or cultivate or plough (soil); to prepare for growing vegetation and crops.

till.ety: From Middle English til, from Northern Old English til, from or akin to Old Norse til (“to, till”); both from Proto-Germanic *til (“to, toward”), from Proto-Germanic *tilą (“planned point in time”). Not a contraction of until; rather, until comes from till with the prefix un- (“against; toward; up to”) also found in unto. Cognate with Old Frisian til (“to, till”), Danish til (“to”), Swedish till (“to, till”), Icelandic til (“to, till”). Also related to Old English til (“good”), German Ziel (“goal”), Gothic 𐍄𐌹𐌻 (til, “something fitting or suitable”).

ex.en: He is late. Let's wait for him till 5:30.
ex.ja: 彼は遅いですね。５時３０分まで待ちましょう。

ex.en: Please wait till five, when he'll be back.
ex.ja: ５時までお待ちください。その頃には彼ももどりますから。

ex.en: He was at work till late at night.
ex.ja: 彼は夜遅くまで仕事をしていた。

note.ja: 「〜まで」は古北欧語 til（〜へ）から。until と同じ。「耕す」は古英語 tilian（努める）からで別語。「レジ」も別語。

en: A distressing or dangerous situation.
A difficulty, problem, condition, or action contributing to such a situation.
To mentally distress; to cause (someone) to be anxious or perplexed.
In weaker sense: to bother or inconvenience.

trouble.ety: Verb is from Middle English troublen, trouble, borrowed from Old French troubler, trobler, trubler, metathetic variants of tourbler, torbler, turbler, from Vulgar Latin *turbulō, from Latin turbula (“disorderly group, a little crowd or people”), diminutive of turba (“stir; crowd”). The noun is from Middle English trouble, troble, from Old French troble, from the verb.

ex.en: I'm sorry that I got you in trouble.
ex.ja: あなたをトラブルに巻き込んでしまってごめんなさい。

ex.en: You need not take the trouble to go.
ex.ja: あえて行くに及ばない。

ex.en: I don't want there to be any trouble.
ex.ja: 私はそこでどんな問題も起こしたくない。

note.ja: ラテン語 turbare（かき乱す）から。turb（かき乱す）。かき乱すこと →「困難・心配・故障」。disturb（ひどくかき乱す→邪魔する）も同じ。

en: Any condition, circumstance, opportunity or means, particularly favorable or chance to success, or to any desired end.
Superiority of state, or that which gives it; benefit; gain; profit
to provide (someone) with an advantage, to give an edge to
to do something for one's own benefit; to take advantage of

ex.en: We have to take advantage of this situation.
ex.ja: 此の状況を利用すべきだ。

ex.en: This frame shows the painting to good advantage.
ex.ja: この額に入れると絵が引き立ちます。

ex.en: It is to your advantage to join us.
ex.ja: 私たちの仲間に入るのが有利だ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 avant（前に）から。ラテン語 ab ante。「前にいること」→「有利・利点」。advance と同じ。

en: Placed separately (in regard to space or time).
Separately, exclusively, not together.
Excluded from consideration.
Exceptional, distinct.
Having been taken apart; disassembled, in pieces.

apart.ety: From Middle English apart, aparte, a-part, a part, from Anglo-Norman a part, from Latin ad partem (“to the side”).

ex.en: He couldn't bear to be apart from her.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女と離れていることに耐えられなかった。

ex.en: He is a teacher apart from the rest.
ex.ja: 彼は他の教師とは別だ。

ex.en: Apart from the plot, the book interested me.
ex.ja: 筋書きは別として、その本は私をひきつけた。

note.ja: a（〜へ）+ part（部分）。部分ごとに分かれて →「離れて・別々に」。apartment（分けられた部屋）も同じ。

en: Vigilant or on one's guard against danger or difficulty.
Conscious or having knowledge of something; awake.

aware.ety: Inherited from Middle English aware, iwar, iware, ywar, from Old English ġewær (“aware”), from Proto-West Germanic *gawar, from Proto-Germanic *waraz (“aware, cautious”), from Proto-Indo-European *worós (“attentive”), from *wer- (“to heed; watch out”). Cognate with Dutch gewaar, German gewahr, Danish var, Swedish var, Icelandic varr.

ex.en: She may not be aware of the danger.
ex.ja: 彼女は危険に気付いていないかもしれない。

ex.en: We were aware of what was going on.
ex.ja: 私たちは何が起きつつあるか気づいていた。

ex.en: I wasn't aware that somebody was watching me.
ex.ja: 誰かが私をみているなんて気づかなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 gewær（用心深い）から。wary、beware と同じ ware。「気づいている」。

en: A mammal of the family Felidae.
A carnivorous, four-legged, generally furry domesticated species (Felis catus) of feline animal, commonly kept as a house pet.
To hoist (an anchor) by its ring so that it hangs at the cathead.
To flog with a cat-o'-nine-tails.
Catastrophic; terrible, disastrous.

cat.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *kattuz
Proto-West Germanic *kattu
Old English catt
Middle English cat
English cat
From Middle English cat, catte, from Old English catt (“male cat”), catte (“female cat”), from Proto-West Germanic *kattu, from Proto-Germanic *kattuz, generally thought to be from Late Latin cattus (“domestic cat”) (c. 350, Palladius), from Latin catta (c. 75 A.D., Martial), possibly from an Afroasiatic language. Doublet of gato.
A loan from Afro-Asiatic into European languages would roughly match how the animal itself spread, as genetic studies suggest domestic cats first began to

ex.en: The question is: Who will bell the cat.
ex.ja: 問題は誰が猫に鈴をつけるかだ。

ex.en: I like dogs and my sister likes cats.
ex.ja: 私は犬が好きで、妹は猫が好きです。

ex.en: I wish that I'd been born a cat.
ex.ja: 猫として生まれたかったなぁ。

note.ja: 後期ラテン語 cattus から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: A person or company who purchases or receives a product or service from a business or merchant or intends to do so.
A person, especially one engaging in some sort of interaction with others.

customer.ety: From Middle English custumer, from Old French coustumier, costumier (compare modern French coutumier), from Medieval Latin custumarius (“a toll-gatherer, tax-collector”, noun), from custumarius (“pertaining to custom or customs”, adjective), from custuma (“custom, tax”). More at custom. By surface analysis, custom + -er.

ex.en: The customer rejected everything that I showed her.
ex.ja: その客は私が見せたものを全部いやだといった。

ex.en: We have a parking lot for the customers.
ex.ja: お客様用の駐車場があります。

ex.en: We sold the store for want of customers.
ex.ja: お客がないので店を売った。

note.ja: custom（習慣）+ -er。「習慣的に店に来る人」→「客」。costume も custom と同じ語源。

en: The main meal of the day, often eaten in the evening.
An evening meal.
To eat a dinner.
To provide (someone) with a dinner.

dinner.ety: From Middle English dyner, from Old French disner (“lunch”, but originally “breakfast”), (modern French dîner), from Vulgar Latin *disiūnō, *disiūnāre from Latin dis- + iēiūnō (“to break the fast”).

ex.en: Why don't we talk about this over dinner?
ex.ja: 夕食を食べながらこのことについて話しませんか。

ex.en: For dinner I only had a little fruit.
ex.ja: 夕食は、果物を少し食べただけよ。

ex.en: I'll call you after I've finished eating dinner.
ex.ja: ご飯が終わったら、電話するね。

note.ja: 古フランス語 disner（朝食をとる）から。ラテン語 dis + jejunare（断食する）。「断食を破る」→ 一日の主な食事。breakfast（break + fast）と同じ発想。

en: Official designation for currency in some parts of the world, including Canada, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hon…
Money generally.

dollar.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *dalą
Proto-West Germanic *dal
Old High German tal
Middle High German tal
German Tal
German Talerder.
Middle Low German dālerbor.
Dutch dalerbor.
English dollar
Attested since the mid-16th century, from early Dutch daler, daalder, from German Taler, Thaler (“dollar”), earlier Joachimsthaler, literally “of Joachimstal”, the town where the original dollars were minted. The name means “(Saint) Joachim's valley”, from Joachim + Tal. Possibly reinforced by the Dutch leeuwendaalder, which was also used in the American colonies. Doublet of taler /thaler and tolar.

ex.en: The money amounts to almost two thousands dollars.
ex.ja: お金はほぼ総計２０００ドルになる。

ex.en: I am not about to pay ten dollars.
ex.ja: 私は１０ドルも払うつもりはない。

ex.en: They charged me five dollars for the bag.
ex.ja: そのかばんの代金として５ドル請求された。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Taler（銀貨）から。ボヘミアのヨアヒムスタール（谷：Thal）産の銀貨にちなむ。

en: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.
Blowing from the east; easterly.

eastern.ety:
From Middle English esturne, esterne, from Old English ēasterne (“eastern”), from Proto-Germanic *austrōnijaz (“eastern”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews-ro- (“eastern”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews- (“dawn, east”). Cognate with Old Saxon and Old High German ōstrōni (“eastern”), Old Norse austrœnn (“eastern”).
Morphologically east + -ern.

ex.en: Japan is in the eastern part of Asia.
ex.ja: 日本はアジアの東部にあります。

ex.en: Japan is located in the eastern part of Asia.
ex.ja: 日本はアジアの東部にあります。

ex.en: The eastern sky was getting light.
ex.ja: 東の空が白み始めていた。

note.ja: east（東）+ -ern。「東の」。

en: The ordinal form of the number five.
The person or thing in the fifth position.
The fifth gear of a transmission.
To sing in the fifth voice in a polyphonic melody.
To support something fifth, after four others have already done so.

fifth.ety:
PIE word
 *pénkʷe
From Middle English fifthe, fifte, fift, from Old English fīfta (“fifth”), from Proto-Germanic *fimftô (“fifth”) or *femftô, equivalent to five + -th (ordinal suffix). Cognate with Scots fift, fyft (“fifth”), North Frisian fyfde (“fifth”), West Frisian fyfde (“fifth”), Dutch vijfde (“fifth”), Low German fifte, föfte, füfte (“fifth”), German fünfte (“fifth”), Danish femte (“fifth”), Swedish femte (“fifth”), Icelandic fimmta (“fifth”).

ex.en: A fire broke out on the fifth floor.
ex.ja: 火事は５階から起きました。

ex.en: I'd like to get off at Fifth Avenue.
ex.ja: ５番街で降りたいのですが。

ex.en: They controlled a fifth part of the territory.
ex.ja: 彼らは領土の５分の１を支配していた。

note.ja: five の序数。古英語 fīfta。

en: What something does or is used for.
A professional or official position.

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ ist（立つ）。外に現れて立つ →「存在する」。insist（上に立つ→主張する）、resist（逆らって立つ→抵抗する）、assist（そばに立つ→助ける）も同じ sist。

en: A place where agricultural and similar activities take place, especially the growing of crops or the raising of livestock.
A tract of land held on lease for the purpose of cultivation.
To work on a farm, especially in the growing and harvesting of crops.
To devote (land) to farming.

farm.ety:
Inherited from Middle English ferme, farme (“rent, revenue, produce, factor, stewardship, meal, feast”), influenced by Anglo-Norman ferme (“rent, lease, farm”), from Medieval Latin ferma, firma.
There is debate as to whether Medieval Latin acquired this term from Old English feorm (“rent, provision, supplies, feast”), from Proto-Germanic *fermō, *firhuma- (“means of living, subsistence”), from Proto-Germanic *ferhwō (“life force, body, being”), from Proto-Indo-European *perkʷ- (“life, force, strength, tree”); or from Latin firmus (“solid, secure”), from Proto-Italic *fermos, from Proto-Indo-Eu

ex.en: My uncle has a farm in the village.
ex.ja: 私の叔父はその村に農園を持っています。

ex.en: They led a happy life on their farm.
ex.ja: 彼らは農場で幸せな日々を送った。

ex.en: The stable is right behind the farm house.
ex.ja: 農家のちょうど後ろに馬小屋がある。

note.ja: 古フランス語 ferme（賃貸契約）から。ラテン語 firmus（確かな）。「固定の地代で借りた土地」→「農場」。firm と同じ。

en: A collection of papers collated and archived together.
A roll or list.
To commit (official papers) to some office.
To submit a formal request to some office.

file.ety: From Old French fil (“thread”), from Latin fīlum (“thread”). Doublet of filum.

ex.en: She filed a suit for divorce against him.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼に対して離婚訴訟を起こした。

ex.en: Have you come to file a damage report?
ex.ja: 被害届を出すためにきたのか？

ex.en: The secretary was asked to file past records.
ex.ja: 秘書は過去の記録をファイルするように頼まれた。

en: To attach; to affix; to hold in place or at a particular time.
To focus or determine (oneself, on a concept); to fixate.
A repair or corrective action.
A difficult situation; a quandary or dilemma; a predicament.

fix.ety: From Middle English fixen, borrowed from Old French *fixer (attested only as ficher, fichier; > English fitch), from fix (“fastened; fixed”), from Latin fīxus (“immovable; steady; stable; fixed”), from fīgō (“to drive in; stick; fasten”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeygʷ- (“to jab; stick; set”). Related to dig.

ex.en: It's no use trying to fix it now.
ex.ja: いまそれを直そうったって無駄だ。

ex.en: He kept his eyes fixed on her face.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女の顔から目を離さなかった。

ex.en: Tom will have that fixed in no time.
ex.ja: トムはすぐにそれを直してしまうだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 fixus（固定された）から。figere（固定する）。「固定する」→「決める」→「修理する」。suffix、prefix と同じ。

en: Any insect of the order Diptera; characterized by having two wings (except for some wingless species), also called true flies.
Especially, any of the insects of the family Muscidae, such as the common housefly (other families of Diptera include mosquitoes and midg…
To travel through the air, another gas, or a vacuum, without being in contact with a grounded surface.
To take a flight on a plane; to pilot or crew a plane.

ex.en: Some pretty birds are flying above the trees.
ex.ja: きれいな鳥が木の上を飛んでいる。

en: Honest, especially in a manner that seems slightly blunt; candid; not reserved or disguised.
Unmistakable, clinically obvious, self-evident.
Free postage, a right exercised by governments (usually with definite article).
The notice on an envelope where a stamp would normally be found.
To place a frank on an envelope.
To exempt from charge for postage, as a letter, package, or packet, etc.

frank.ety: From Middle English frank, from Old French franc (“free”), in turn from the name of an early Germanic confederation, the Franks, from Proto-West Germanic *frankō (“javelin, spear”). Doublet of Frank, franc, and farang.

ex.en: He is quite frank with me about everything.
ex.ja: 彼はどんなことでも私に全く隠しだてしない。

ex.en: She was at once frank and honest.
ex.ja: 彼女は率直でもあり素直でもあった。

ex.en: Americans are frank enough to say what they think.
ex.ja: アメリカ人は思っている事を率直に言う。

en: Someone who guides, especially someone hired to show people around a place or an institution and offer information and explanation, or to…
A document or book that offers information or instruction; guidebook.
To serve as a guide for someone or something; to lead or direct in a way; to conduct in a course or path.
To steer or navigate, especially a ship or as a pilot.

ex.en: A guide conducted the visitors round the museum.
ex.ja: ガイドは観光客に博物館の案内をした。

ex.en: Can I hire a guide who speaks Japanese?
ex.ja: 日本語のガイドを雇うことができますか。

ex.en: The guide told the kids not to take pictures.
ex.ja: ガイドは子供たちに写真は撮ってはいけませんと言った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 guider から。ゲルマン語 wit（知る）と同系。「道を知る人」→「案内人」。

en: The act of investigating; the process of inquiring into or following up; research, especially patient or thorough inquiry or examination

investigation.ety: From Middle English investigacioun, from Old French investigacion, from Latin investigatio. Morphologically investigate + -ion.

ex.en: I don't want the investigation to burn out.
ex.ja: 捜査を立ち消えにしてほしくない。

ex.en: We conducted our investigation with the greatest care.
ex.ja: 私たちはきわめて慎重に調査を行なった。

ex.en: The cause of the accident is still under investigation.
ex.ja: 事故の原因はまだ捜索中だ。

note.ja: investigate（調査する）+ -ion。in + vestigium（足跡）。「足跡をたどること」→「調査」。

en: To perform a work or labour; to exert power or strength, physical or mechanical; to act.
To produce an effect.

ex.en: I installed an operating system on my computer.
ex.ja: 自分のパソコンにOSをインストールしました。

ex.en: The patient was operated on in the morning.
ex.ja: その患者は午前中に手術を受けたんだ。

ex.en: This store is operated on a cash basis.
ex.ja: この店は現金取り引きが原則です。

note.ja: oper（仕事）+ ate。仕事をする →「操作する・作動する・手術する」。

en: The state of being responsible, accountable, or answerable.
The state of being liable, culpable, or responsible for something in particular.

responsibility.ety: From responsible + -ity. Although the components are of French origin, the compound appears to have been formed in English. Later-attested French responsabilité is modeled on the English word, and Italian responsabilità is in turn modeled on the French.

ex.en: In brief, you should have accepted the responsibility.
ex.ja: つまり君が責任を取るべきだったのだ。

ex.en: It isn't like anybody takes responsibility then anyway.
ex.ja: そして誰が責任をとるわけでもない。

ex.en: I'm surprised by her lack of responsibility.
ex.ja: 彼女の無責任さには呆れてしまう。

note.ja: re（返して）+ spons（約束する）+ ibility。約束を返す（応える）能力 →「責任」。

en: To revolve by turning over and over; to move by turning on a horizontal axis; to impel forward with a revolving motion on a supporting su…
To wrap (something) round on itself; to form into a spherical or cylindrical body by causing to turn over and over.
The act or result of rolling, or state of being rolled.
Something formed into a compact shape by being rolled up.

roll.ety:
From Middle English rollen, partly from Old French roller, roler, röeler, röoler, from Medieval Latin rotulāre (“to roll; to revolve”), from Latin rotula (“a little wheel”), diminutive of rota (“a wheel”); partly from Anglo-Latin rollāre, from the same ultimate source.
Displaced native English welt and partially displaced English wallow.

ex.en: Tom is on the honor roll, isn't he?
ex.ja: トムは成績優秀者だよね？

ex.en: I'd like a roll of color film, please.
ex.ja: カラーフィルムを一本ください。

ex.en: He was the king of rock-and-roll.
ex.ja: 彼はロックンロールの帝王だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 rotula（小さな車輪）から。rota（車輪）。「転がる」→「巻いたもの」→「名簿」。role（巻物の台本）、control と同じ。

en: Slenderly; delicately.
To a small extent or degree.

From slight + -ly.

ex.en: But his name is slightly familiar to me.
ex.ja: でも名前くらいは知っている。

ex.en: Ten people were slightly injured in the accident.
ex.ja: その事故で１０人が軽いけがをした。

ex.en: He was slightly injured in a traffic accident.
ex.ja: 彼は交通事故で軽傷を負った。

note.ja: slight（わずかな）+ -ly。「少し」。

en: To imply but stop short of explicitly stating (something).
To cause one to suppose (something); to bring to one's mind the idea (of something).

suggest.ety: Coined based on Latin suggestus, perfect passive participle of suggerō (“bring up, bring under, lay beneath, furnish, supply, excite, advise, suggest”, verb), from sub (“from below, under”) + gerō (“bear, carry”, verb).

ex.en: He suggested to us that we should go.
ex.ja: 彼は私たちに、行きましょうと言った。

ex.en: He suggested to us that we should stay.
ex.ja: 彼は私たちにとどまるように示唆した。

ex.en: Mother suggested that I write her at once.
ex.ja: 母は私がすぐに彼女に手紙を書くよう提案した。

note.ja: sug（下から）+ gest（運ぶ）。下からそっと運び出す →「提案する・示唆する」。digest（ばらばらに運ぶ→消化する）、gesture（運び方→身振り）も同じ gest。

en: Something unexpected.
A mess of feces, left by a pet or small child in an unexpected place or at an unexpected time.
To cause (someone) to feel unusually alarmed or delighted by something unexpected.
To do something to (a person) that they are not expecting, as a surprise.
Drawing attention to a surprising action by oneself.
Drawing attention to something that should have been obvious.

surprise.ety: From Middle English surprise, borrowed from Middle French surprise (“an overtake”), nominal use of the past participle of Old French sorprendre (“to overtake”), from sor- (“over”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin super- + Latin prendere, contracted from prehendere (“to grasp, seize”). Doublet of suppli.

ex.en: I thought you might be a little surprised.
ex.ja: あなたがちょっと驚くのではないかと思っていました。

ex.en: The old man looked surprised at the news.
ex.ja: 老人はその知らせに驚いたようだった。

ex.en: It's not much of a surprise, is it?
ex.ja: そんなに驚くことじゃないよね？

note.ja: sur（上から）+ pris（つかむ）。上から不意につかみかかる →「驚かせる」。enterprise（事業）、comprise（含む）も同じ prehend。

en: Specifically related to a particular discipline.
difficult to understand for those not specialized in this discipline.
A pickup truck with a gun mounted on it.
A special move in certain fighting games that cancels out the effect of an opponent's attack.

technical.ety:
From Late Latin technicus + -al, from Ancient Greek τεχνικός (tekhnikós), from τέχνη (tékhnē, “skill”).
For the late 20th-century origin of the noun sense (vehicle), see Wikipedia.

ex.en: You should go on to a technical college.
ex.ja: あなたは理科系の大学に進んだほうがいいよ。

ex.en: This technical journal is above me.
ex.ja: この専門紙は私には理解できない。

ex.en: Written in technical terms, this book is very difficult to understand.
ex.ja: 専門用語で書いてあるため、この本は実に読みにくい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 techne（技術）から。tech + nic + al。技術の →「技術的な・専門的な」。

en: To negotiate, discuss terms, bargain (for or with).
To discourse; to handle a subject in writing or speaking; to conduct a discussion.
An entertainment, outing, food, drink, or other indulgence provided by someone for the enjoyment of others.
An unexpected gift, event etc., which provides great pleasure.

treat.ety: From Middle English treten, from Anglo-Norman treter, Old French tretier, traiter, from Latin tractāre (“to pull", "to manage”), from the past participle stem of trahere (“to draw", "to pull”).

ex.en: We are tired of being treated like children.
ex.ja: 私たちは子供扱いされるのにはうんざりだ。

ex.en: She treated me to a cup of tea.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に紅茶を１杯ふるまってくれた。

ex.en: Don't treat me like I am a disease.
ex.ja: ばい菌扱いするなよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 tractare（扱う）から。tract（引く）。引き回して扱う →「扱う・治療する・おごる」。treaty（取り扱いの取り決め→条約）も同じ。

en: Being the only one of its kind; unequaled, unparalleled or unmatched.
Of a feature, such that only one holder has it.
A thing without a like; something unequalled or unparallelled; one of a kind.

unique.ety: Borrowed from French unique, from Latin unicus.

ex.en: This is a plant unique to this country.
ex.ja: これはこの国に特有の植物だ。

ex.en: Unique ideas helped him to earn a high income.
ex.ja: 独特のアイディアのおかげで、彼は高い収入を得た。

ex.en: His technique was unique and absolutely amazing.
ex.ja: 彼の技術は独特で、本当に驚くべきものだった。

ex.ja: その会社は様々な商品を扱っている。

ex.ja: もっと仕事に変化があったならばなあ。

Physical action which causes destruction, harm, pain, or suffering.

ex.en: There is almost no violence in that city.
ex.ja: その市にはほとんど暴力事件はない。

ex.en: Non-violence is the first article of my faith.
ex.ja: 非暴力というのは私の信仰の第１条だ。

ex.en: I can't put up with his violence any longer.
ex.ja: 彼の暴力にもうがまんできない。

en: An instrument of attack or defense in combat or hunting, e.g. most guns, missiles, or swords.
An instrument or other means of harming or exerting control over another.
To equip with a weapon; to arm.

weapon.ety:
From Middle English wepen, from Old English wǣpn, from Proto-West Germanic *wāpn, from Proto-Germanic *wēpną (“weapon”), of unknown origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *wēbnom.
Cognates
Cognate with Scots weepon (“weapon”), North Frisian woopen (“weapon”), Saterland Frisian Woapen (“weapon”), West Frisian wapen (“weapon; coat of arms”), Alemannic German Waaffe (“tool”), Dutch wapen (“weapon”), German Waffe (“weapon”) and Wappen (“coat of arms”), Luxembourgish Waff (“weapon”), Yiddish וואָפֿן (vofn, “weapon”), Danish våben (“weapon; coat of arms”), Faroese vákn, vápn (“weapon; whaling lan

ex.en: We think nuclear weapons will destroy our earth.
ex.ja: 核兵器はわが地球を滅ぼすと思う。

ex.en: Japan should not spend much money on weapons.
ex.ja: 日本は兵器にあまりお金を使うべきではない。

ex.en: It's against the law to carry weapons.
ex.ja: 武器を持ち歩くのは法律違反である。

note.ja: 古英語 wǣpen から。「武器」。

en: The quality or state of being young.
The part of life following childhood; the period of existence preceding maturity or age; the whole early part of life, from childhood, or…

youth.ety: From Middle English youthe, youghte, ȝouþe, from Old English ġeoguþ (“the state of being young; youth”), from Proto-West Germanic *juwunþa, from Proto-Germanic *jugunþō, *jugunþiz (“youth”), corresponding to young + -th (abstract nominal suffix). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Juugd, West Frisian jeugd, Dutch jeugd, German Low German Jöögd, German Jugend.

ex.en: He grew up to be a fine youth.
ex.ja: 彼は成長してりっぱな若者になった。

ex.en: He was a hard worker in his youth.
ex.ja: 若いときは、彼は働き者であった。

ex.en: In his youth, he had shown great promise.
ex.ja: 若い時、彼はおおいに有望だった。

en: To be grateful or thankful for.
To view as valuable.

appreciate.ety:
Originated 1645–55; from Medieval Latin appreciātus (“valued or appraised”), later variant of Late Latin appretiātus (“appraised”), the perfect passive participle of appretiō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from a(d) (“toward”) + preti(um) (“price”) + -ō (first conjugation verb-forming suffix).
Cognate to French apprécier. Latin root also origin of English appraise, which has various Romance cognates; see also precious.

ex.en: I'd appreciate it if you could do that.
ex.ja: そうしてもらえると助かります。

ex.en: I deeply appreciate your coming all the way.
ex.ja: はるばるおいでいただいて深く感謝いたします。

ex.en: I appreciate it, but I think I shouldn't.
ex.ja: ありがとう、でも遠慮しておきます。

note.ja: ラテン語 appretiare ＝ ad + pretium（値段）。「値をつける」→「価値を認める」→「正しく理解する・感謝する」。price、precious と同じ。

en: To find or learn something for the first time.
To create by moving a piece out of another piece's line of attack.

discover.ety: From Middle English discoveren, from Old French descovrir, from Late Latin discoperīre < discooperiō, discooperīre, from Latin dis- + cooperiō. Displaced native Old English onfindan.

ex.en: He discovered that he had made a mistake.
ex.ja: 彼は間違いをしたことが分かった。

ex.en: Oil has been discovered under the North Sea.
ex.ja: 北海の海底で石油が発見されている。

ex.en: The diamond was discovered by a boy in 1873.
ex.ja: そのダイヤは１８７３年に、ある少年によって発見された。

note.ja: dis（取り去る）+ cover（覆う）。「覆いを取る」→「発見する」。

en: Free from or lacking moisture.
Unable to produce a liquid, as water, (petrochemistry) oil, or (agriculture) milk.
The process by which something is dried.
A prohibitionist (of alcoholic beverages).
To lose moisture.
To remove moisture from.

The verb derives from Middle English drien, from Old English drȳġan (“to dry”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgijan, from Proto-Germanic *drūgiz (“hard, desiccated, dry”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerǵʰ- (“strong, hard, solid”).
cognates and related terms
 Cognate with Scots dry, drey (“dry”),

ex.en: Dry your hair! You will catch a cold.
ex.ja: 髪乾かしなよ。風邪ひくよ。

ex.en: The paint on the door isn't dry yet.
ex.ja: このドアのペンキはまだ乾いていない。

ex.en: Give me a cut, wash and dry please.
ex.ja: カットして、洗髪して、乾燥してください。

note.ja: 古英語 drȳge から。drought（日照り）と同系。

A one-dimensional face of a polytope. In particular, the joining line between two vertices of a polygon; the place where two faces of a p…
To move an object slowly and carefully in a particular direction.
To move slowly and carefully in a particular direction.

ex.ja: 米国は民主国家である。

The act of describing; a delineation by marks or signs.

en: Having excelled, having surpassed.
Of higher or the highest quality; splendid.

excellent.ety: From Middle English excellent, from Old French excellent, from Latin excellēns (“elevated, exalted”), present participle of excellō (“elevate, exult”), equivalent to excel + -ent.

ex.ja: 今夜のパーティーで彼は見事にホスト役を演じた。

ex.ja: 僕は、彼をすばらしい先生だと考えている。

To keep watch over, in order to prevent escape or restrain from acts of violence, or the like.

ex.ja: その警備員は一晩中勤務だった。

en: Scrupulous with regard to telling the truth; not given to swindling, lying, or fraud; upright.
True, especially as far as is known by the person making the statement; fair; unbiased.
Honestly; really.

honest.ety: From Middle English honest, honeste (“honourable, appropriate, excellent”), from Old French honeste, from Latin honestus, from honor. ex.ja: 私には彼は正直なように思われる。

ex.ja: 彼女は誠実だから嘘をついたりしない。

ex.ja: 私たちはトムが正直者だと考える。

note.ja: ラテン語 honestus（名誉ある）から。honos（名誉）。honor と同じ。

en: A protected cove or harbor, out of the wind.
The side of the ship away from the wind.
Facing away from the flow of a fluid, usually air.

lee.ety: From Middle English lee, from Old English hlēo, hlēow (“shelter, protection”), from Proto-West Germanic *hlaiw (whence also Proto-Slavic *xlěvъ), from Proto-Germanic *hlaiwaz (compare German Lee (“lee”), Swedish lä, Danish læ, Norwegian le, Old Norse hlé, Dutch lij), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱley- (compare Welsh clyd (“warm, cozy”), Latin calēre (“to warm up”), Lithuanian šiltas (“warm, pleasant”), Sanskrit शरद् (śarad, “autumn”)).

ex.en: He proposed to Miss Lee and she accepted.
ex.ja: 彼がリー嬢に結婚を申し込んだところ、彼女は承諾した。

ex.ja: 「ええ、わかったわ」とリー夫人が言う。

en: A substance which specifically promotes healing when ingested or consumed in some way; a pharmaceutical drug.
Any treatment or cure.

medicine.ety: From Middle English medicin, from Middle French medicine, from Old French medecine, from Latin medicīna (“the healing art, medicine, a physician's shop, a remedy, medicine”), feminine of medicīnus (“of or belonging to physic or surgery, or to a physician or surgeon”), from medicus (“a physician, surgeon”). The extended sense of "Indigenous magic" is a calque of Ojibwe mashkiki (“medicine”) or mide (or cognates in related languages) when used in compounds such as Grand Medicine Society, medicine lodge, medicine dance, medicine bag, medicine wheel, medicine man, Medicine Line, and bad medicine o

ex.ja: 一体なんで薬を飲まなかったの？

ex.ja: 新薬のおかげで私は病気から回復した。

ex.en: You'll feel better if you drink this medicine.
ex.ja: この薬を飲めば、気分が良くなりますよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 medicina（医術）から。medicus（医者）。「医学・薬」。medical と同じ。

en: An elevation of land of considerable dimensions rising more or less abruptly, forming a conspicuous figure in the landscape, usually havi…
Something very large in size or quantity; a huge amount; a great heap.

mountain.ety: From Middle English mountayne, mountain, montaigne, from Anglo-Norman muntaine, muntaigne, from Early Medieval Latin montānia, a collective based on Latin montem (“mountain”), from Proto-Indo-European *monti (compare Welsh mynydd (“mountain”), Albanian mat (“bank, shore”), Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬙𐬌 (mati, “promontory”)), from *men- (“to project, stick out”). Displaced native English barrow (from Old English beorg) and down (from Old English dūn), and partially displaced non-native Old English munt, from Latin mōns (whence English mount).

ex.en: Finally, we reached the top of the mountain.
ex.ja: とうとう私達は山の頂上に到着した。

ex.en: We finally reached the top of the mountain.
ex.ja: とうとう私達は山の頂上に到着した。

ex.en: That is the highest mountain in the world.
ex.ja: あれは世界一高い山です。

note.ja: ラテン語 mons（山）から古フランス語を経た語。mount、Montana と同じ mont。

en: Pertaining to the nucleus of an atom.
Involving energy released by nuclear reactions (fission, fusion, radioactive decay).
Nuclear power.
Nuclear weapon

nuclear.ety: From Latin nū̆cleus, a contraction of the adjective nuculeus, masculine of feminine nuculea (“pertaining to a small nut”) from nucula + adjectival suffix -eus, -ea, -eum. The Latin nucula + -āris adds up to nuculāris, a term that in English becomes nucular; the Latin nuculea + -āris, becomes Latin nuculeāris (“relative to what pertains to small nut”), later contracted into nuclear. By surface analysis, nucleus + -ar. Compare muscle and Latin mūsculus; muscular and mūsculāris.

ex.en: We think nuclear weapons will destroy our earth.
ex.ja: 核兵器はわが地球を滅ぼすと思う。

ex.en: The question is how to avoid nuclear war.
ex.ja: 問題は、いかに核戦争を避けるかである。

ex.en: Nuclear power plants don't appeal to everybody.
ex.ja: 原子力発電所はすべての人に訴えるわけではない。

en: A place on the coast at which ships can shelter, or dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
A town or city containing such a place, a port city.
Of or relating to port, the left-hand side of a vessel when facing the bow.
To turn or put to the left or larboard side of a ship; said of the helm.
To dock at a port.

ex.ja: 船はやっと母港についた。

ex.en: Could you tell me the way to the port?
ex.ja: 港へはどう行ったらいいのか教えてください。

note.ja: ラテン語 portus（港）から。「運ぶ（portare）」と同じ祖先。物が運ばれる場所 →「港」。airport（空の港→空港）、passport（港を通る許可）も仲間。

en: The fact or condition of being present, or of being within sight or call, or at hand.
The part of space within one's immediate vicinity.
To make or become present.

presence.ety: Through Old French presence, from Latin praesentia (“a being present”), from praesentem. Displaced native Old English andweardnes.

ex.en: He was calm in the presence of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても冷静だった。

ex.en: She tried to keep her presence of mind.
ex.ja: 彼女は落ち着きを保とうと努めた。

ex.en: You should better not smoke in his presence.
ex.ja: 彼の前では煙草を吸わない方がいいですよ。

note.ja: present（そこにいる）+ -ence。prae（前に）+ esse（ある）。「目の前にあること」→「存在」。

en: An action or statement in response to a stimulus or other event.
A transformation in which one or more substances is converted into another by combination or decomposition.

reaction.ety: Inherited from Middle English reaccion, from Old French reaction, from Latin reāctiō, from the verb reagō, from re- (“again”) + agō (“to act”); more at re-, action; equivalent to react + -ion.

ex.en: What was their reaction to the report?
ex.ja: 報告書に対する彼らの反応はどうでしたか。

ex.en: What was his reaction to this news?
ex.ja: このニュースに対する彼の反応はどうでしたか。

ex.en: What was her reaction to the news?
ex.ja: このニュースに対する彼女の反応はどうでしたか。

note.ja: re（返して）+ act（行う）+ ion。行いを返すこと →「反応・反動」。

en: To bring down the size, quantity, quality, value or intensity of something; to diminish, to lower.
To lose weight.

From Middle English reducen, from Old French reduire, from Latin redūcō (“reduce”); from re- (“back”) + dūcō (“lead”). See duke, and compare with redoubt.

ex.en: I've reduced the amount of meat I eat.
ex.ja: 私は肉を食べるのを控えた。

ex.en: Mass production reduced the price of many goods.
ex.ja: 大量生産が多くの商品価格を下げた。

ex.en: Therefore, it is necessary to reduce the cost.
ex.ja: したがって生産費を削る必要がある。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ ducere（導く）。「元に戻す」→「減らす」。produce、introduce と同じ duc。

Appreciably large in size, quantity, or value.
Solidly.
Without spaces or hyphens.
A substance in the fundamental state of matter that retains its size and shape without need of a container (as opposed to a liquid or gas).
A three-dimensional figure (as opposed to a surface, an area, or a curve).

Aggression toward an organism resulting in a response in an attempt to restore previous conditions.
To apply force to (a body or structure) causing strain.
To apply emotional pressure to (a person or animal).

To sample the flavor of something orally.

en: The tea plant (Camellia sinensis); (countable) a variety of this plant.
The dried leaves or buds of the tea plant; (countable) a variety of such leaves.
To drink tea.
To take afternoon tea (a light meal).

ex.ja: この勝利に対して我々は大変な代価を払った。

en: The part of the day from noon or lunchtime until sunset, evening, or suppertime or 6pm.
The later part of anything, often with implications of decline.

afternoon.ety: From Middle English afternone, after-non, equivalent to after- + noon.

ex.en: I will be all tied up tomorrow afternoon.
ex.ja: 私は明日の午後はふさがっている。

ex.en: I studied for a while in the afternoon.
ex.ja: 私は午後しばらくの間勉強した。

ex.en: I have been reading the book all afternoon.
ex.ja: 私は午後ずっとその本を読み続けている。

note.ja: after（後の）+ noon（正午）。「正午の後」→「午後」。

en: Having a subordinate or auxiliary position.
Helping; lending aid or support; auxiliary.
A person who assists or helps someone else.
Sales assistant.

en: A resident of a city or town, especially one with legally recognized rights or duties.
A legally recognized member of a state, with associated rights and obligations; a person considered in terms of this role.

ex.ja: 彼は、アメリカ国民になった。

ex.ja: 彼女は老人に席を譲った。

ex.ja: この村にはお年寄りの方が大勢います。

en: Of or relating to the first class or rank, especially in literature or art.
Exemplary of a particular style; defining a class or category; typical; archetypical; epitomic.
A perfect and/or early example of a particular style.
An artistic work of lasting worth, such as a film or song; a work of enduring excellence.

classic.ety: From French classique, from Latin classic(us) (“relating to the classes of Roman citizenry, especially the highest”), from classis. By surface analysis, class + -ic. Piecewise doublet of classy.

ex.ja: どんなに高くてもあのクラシックカーを手に入れたい。

ex.en: Milton is one of the classic writers.
ex.ja: ミルトンは一流作家の人です。

ex.en: Almost no students get full marks in Chinese classics.
ex.ja: 漢文の試験で満点を取る生徒はほとんどいません。

note.ja: ラテン語 classicus（最上級の市民の）から。classis（階級）。「一流の」→「古典」。class と同じ。

en: Items of clothing; apparel.
The covering of a bed; bedclothes.

clothes.ety: From Middle English clothes, cloþes (plural of cloth, cloþ (“cloth, garment”)), from Old English clāþas (“clothes”, plural of clāþ (“cloth”)), equivalent to cloth + -es. ex.ja: 服装で人を判断してはいけない。

Of or relating to an electronic version of a musical instrument that has an acoustic equivalent.
Electricity; the electricity supply.
An electric toothbrush.

electric.ety: First attested in c. 1646 in a publication by Thomas Browne. From New Latin ēlectricus (“electrical; of amber”), from ēlectr(um) (“amber”) + -icus (“adjectival suffix”); from Ancient Greek ἤλεκτρον (ḗlektron, “amber”); related to ἠλέκτωρ (ēléktōr, “shining sun”), of unknown origin (see which for more). The Latin term was apparently used first with the sense electrical in 1600 by the English physician and scientist William Gilbert in his work De Magnete.

ex.en: The discovery of electric waves made radio possible.
ex.ja: 電波の発見により、無線通信が可能になった。

ex.en: This machine is driven by a small electric motor.
ex.ja: この機械は小さな電気モーターで作動する。

ex.en: The performance of electric cars has improved.
ex.ja: 電気自動車の性能はよくなっている。

en: A situation which poses an immediate risk and which requires urgent attention.
The department of a hospital that treats emergencies.

emergency.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin emergentia, from Latin emergens, present participle of emergo (“to emerge, arise, come forth”), equivalent to emergent + -cy or emerge + -ency. Doublet of emergence.

ex.en: In case of an emergency, call the police.
ex.ja: 緊急の場合は警察を呼びなさい。

ex.en: In case of an emergency, push this button.
ex.ja: 緊急の場合は、このボタンを押しなさい。

ex.en: The journalist was calm even in an emergency.
ex.ja: その記者は緊急事態のときでも落ち着いていた。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ merg（浸る）+ ency。水中から外へ浮かび上がってくること →（急に現れる事態）→「緊急事態」。merge（溶け込む→合併する）も同じ。

en: To the full or entire extent.
To the exclusion of others; solely.

entirely.ety: From Middle English entyerly, entierly, enterely, entyreliche, equivalent to entire + -ly.

ex.en: These meetings are carried on entirely in English.
ex.ja: これらの会合は全部英語で行われる。

ex.en: Your guess is entirely off the mark.
ex.ja: 君の推測はまったく的外れだ。

ex.en: He was entirely free of his worry.
ex.ja: 彼の心配はすっかりなくなっていた。

note.ja: entire（全体の）+ -ly。ラテン語 integer（完全な）。「完全に」。integrity と同じ。

en: State or condition of not meeting a desirable or intended objective, opposite of success.
A condition in which a specified organ does not function well enough to support life.

failure.ety: From Anglo-Norman failer, from Old French faillir (“to fail”). Equivalent to fail + -ure.

ex.en: I was surprised to hear of his failure.
ex.ja: 私は彼の失敗を聞いて驚いた。

ex.en: What is the cause of such a failure?
ex.ja: その失敗の原因は何？

ex.en: The reasons for our failure are as follows.
ex.ja: 私たちの失敗の理由は次のとおりです。

en: Pertaining to a feast or feast day; festive. (Now only as the noun used attributively.)
A feast or feast day.
An event or series of special events centred on the celebration or promotion of some theme or aspect of the community, often held at regu…

festival.ety: From Middle English festival (adjective), from Old French festival (“festive”), from Late Latin fēstīvālis, from Latin fēstīvus (“festive”). By surface analysis, festive + -al. Displaced native Old English frēols. The noun is shortened from festival day, from Middle English festival dai, festiuall day (“feast day, festival”).

ex.en: She made friends with them at the school festival.
ex.ja: 彼女は学園祭で彼らと親しくなった。

ex.en: I would like to see the festival.
ex.ja: そのお祭りを見たいのですが。

ex.en: We celebrate the Star Festival in July.
ex.ja: 七夕は七月に祝う。

note.ja: ラテン語 festivus（祝祭の）から。festum（祭り）。feast と同じ。

en: Having no variations in height.
In a horizontal line or plane; not sloping.
So as to be flat.
Completely, firmly, or unequivocally.
An area of level ground (sometimes covered with shallow or tidal water).
Level ground in general.
To become flat or flattened; to sink or fall to an even surface.
To fall from the pitch.

flat.ety:
Etymology tree

English flat
From Middle English flat, a borrowing from Old Norse flatr (compare Norwegian and Swedish flat, Danish flad), from Proto-Germanic *flataz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“flat”); akin to Saterland Frisian flot (“smooth”), German Flöz (“a geological layer”), Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús), Latvian plats, Sanskrit प्रथस् (prathas, “extension”). Doublet of plat and pleyt.
The noun is from Middle English flat (“level piece of ground, flat edge of a weapon”), from the adjective.
The algebraic sense was coi

ex.en: Please drink the beer before it goes flat.
ex.ja: 気が抜けないうちにビールを飲んで下さい。

ex.en: Life is very flat in a small village.
ex.ja: 小さな村では生活はひどく単調です。

ex.en: I live in a flat above a shop.
ex.ja: 私は店舗の二階に住んでいる。

en: Substance consumed to provide energy through combustion, or through chemical or nuclear reaction.
Substance that provides nourishment for a living organism; food.
To provide with fuel.
To exacerbate, to cause to grow or become greater.

fuel.ety: From Middle English fuayle, from Old French fouaille, feuaille (“firewood, kindling”), from feu (“fire”), from Late Latin focus (“fire”), from Latin focus (“hearth”), whence English focus. Cognate with Spanish fuego (“fire”), and Portuguese fogo (“fire”).

ex.en: We're running short of fuel for the winter.
ex.ja: 冬に向けての燃料が不足している。

ex.en: Millions of trees have been cut down for fuel.
ex.ja: 何百万という木が切り倒されて燃料になった。

ex.en: Fuel economy is a big advantage of this car.
ex.ja: 燃料の節約がこの自動車の大きな特長だ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 fouaille（たきぎ）から。ラテン語 focus（炉）。「燃料」→（感情を）あおる。focus と同じ。

en: A greeting (salutation) said when meeting someone or acknowledging someone’s arrival or presence.
A greeting used when answering the telephone.
"Hello!" or an equivalent greeting.
To greet (someone) with "hello".

hello.ety:
First attested in 1826. From holla, hollo (attested 1588). This variant of hallo is often credited to Thomas Edison as a coinage for telephone use, but its appearance in print predates the invention of the telephone by several decades.
Ultimately from a variant of Old English ēalā, such as hēlā, which was used colloquially at the time similarly to how hey and (in some dialects) hi are used nowadays. Thus, equivalent to a compound of hey and lo. Used when drawing attention to yourself.
Possibly influenced by Old Saxon halo, imperative of halōn (“to call, fetch”), used in hailing a ferryman, aki

ex.en: Please say hello to your wife for me.
ex.ja: 奥様にもよろしくおっしゃってください。

ex.en: How many languages can you say "Hello" in?
ex.ja: 何ヵ国語で「こんにちは」って言えますか？

ex.en: But the first thing we say is "hello."
ex.ja: しかし、私たちが口にする第一声は「こんにちは」だ。

note.ja: hollo（おーい）の変化形。電話の普及で「もしもし」「こんにちは」に。

en: Indicative of unkind or malevolent intentions; harsh, cruel.
Unpropitious, unkind, faulty, not up to reasonable standard.
Not well; imperfectly, badly
Trouble; distress; misfortune; adversity.
Harm or injury.

ill.ety:
From Middle English ille (“evil; wicked”), from Old Norse íllr (adjective), ílla (adverb), ílt (noun), from Proto-Germanic *ilhilaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁elḱ- (whence Latin ulcus (“sore”), Ancient Greek ἕλκος (hélkos, “wound, ulcer”), Sanskrit अर्शस् (árśas, “hemorrhoids”)).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots and Yola ill, Danish ilde (“bad”), Faroese, Icelandic illur (“bad, ill, wicked”), Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk ille (“bad”), Swedish illa (“badly; poorly”).

ex.en: I've never heard him speak ill of others.
ex.ja: 彼が他人の悪口を言うのを聞いたことがありません。

ex.en: I never thought that he could be ill.
ex.ja: まさか彼が病気だなんて思わなかった。

ex.en: His delay made the situation all the worse.
ex.ja: 彼が遅れたので事態はますます悪くなった。

Spatially first, placed at the beginning, in the first position; especially said of the first letter of a word.
The first letter of a word or a name, especially of a person's full name (their initials).
A distinguished initial letter of a chapter or section of a document.
To sign one's initial(s), as an abbreviated signature.

ex.ja: イニシャルをサインしてご返送ください。

en: To cause (someone) to be acquainted (with someone else).
To make (something or someone) known, such as by formal announcement or recommendation.

introduce.ety: From Middle English introducen, from Old French introduire, from Latin intrōdūcō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁énteros (“inner, what is inside”) and *dewk-.

ex.ja: あなた方に妻を紹介させてください。

ex.ja: 初めに3分程度で自己紹介をお願いします。

ex.ja: 写真を見せながら紹介します。

note.ja: intro（中へ）+ ducere（導く）。「中へ導き入れる」→「紹介する・導入する」。reduce と同じ duc。

en: To strike or hit with the foot or other extremity of the leg.
To make a sharp jerking movement of the leg, as to strike something.
A hit or strike with the leg, foot or knee.
The action of swinging a foot or leg.

kick.ety: From Middle English kyken (“to strike out with the foot”), from Old Norse kikna (“to sink at the knees”) and keikja (“to bend backwards”) (compare Old Norse keikr (“bent backwards, the belly jutting forward”)), from Proto-Germanic *kaikaz (“bent backwards”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Germanic *kī-, *kij- (“to split, dodge, swerve sidewards”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵeyH- (“to sprout, shoot”). ex.en: He kicked the ball out of the ground.
ex.ja: 彼はボールを運動場の外へ蹴った。

ex.en: He kicked the dog which ran at him.
ex.ja: 彼は自分に向かって走ってきた犬を蹴った。

ex.en: He stopped a moment to kick a rock.
ex.ja: 彼はちょっと立ち止まって小石を蹴飛ばした。

note.ja: 中英語 kiken から。語源ははっきりしない。「蹴る」→ 蹴られたような衝撃 →「スリル」。

en: A bag or wallet.
A bag containing letters to be delivered by post.
To send (a letter, parcel, etc.) through the mail.
To send by electronic mail.

ex.en: How much will it cost by sea mail?
ex.ja: 船便だといくらになりますか。

ex.ja: これらの手紙を投函することを忘れていたら注意してくれませんか。

ex.en: I hope that I receive mail from him.
ex.ja: 彼からメールが来ないかな。

en: Very large in size or extent.
Substantial in mass; bulky, heavy and solid.
A homogeneous mass of rock, not layered and without an obvious crystal structure.

massive.ety: From Middle English massif, from Middle French massif, equivalent to mass + -ive. The Irish sense is possibly derived from Irish mas (“fine, handsome”).

ex.en: We came up against massive popular resistance.
ex.ja: 我々は大掛かりな大衆の抵抗に直面した。

en: Two alike or identical things taken together; often followed by of.
One of the constituent items that make up a pair.
To group into one or more sets of two.
to link two electronic devices wirelessly together, especially through a protocol such as Bluetooth.

pair.ety: From Middle English paire, from Old French paire, from Latin paria (“equals”), neuter plural of par (“pair”). Related to pār (“equal”, adjective). Compare Saterland Frisian Poor (“pair”), West Frisian pear (“pair”), Dutch paar (“pair”), German Paar (“pair”), Italian paio (“pair”)

ex.en: She gave me a nice pair of shoes.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に素晴らしいくつを一足くれた。

ex.en: He received a pair of shoes for nothing.
ex.ja: 彼はただで靴をもらった。

ex.en: He bought a pair of black shoes yesterday.
ex.ja: 彼は昨日黒いくつを１足買った。

note.ja: ラテン語 par（等しい）から。等しいものの組 →「一対・ペア」。compare（比べる）も同じ par。

en: Of a surface: flat or level.
A level or flat surface.
A flat surface extending infinitely in all directions (e.g. horizontal or vertical plane); a bounded portion thereof.
To smooth (wood) with a plane.

ex.en: The plane was late because of bad weather.
ex.ja: 悪天候のため飛行機は延着した。

ex.en: The plane was late due to bad weather.
ex.ja: 悪天候のため飛行機は延着した。

ex.en: Our plane took off exactly at 6 p.m.
ex.ja: 私たちの飛行機は午後六時ちょうどに離陸した。

en: A more-than-adequate amount; plenitude; a great deal.
More than enough.
More than sufficiently.
Used as an intensifier, very.

plenty.ety: From Anglo-Norman plent(é) + -y, from Middle English plentie, plentee, plente, from Anglo-Norman plenté, from Old French plenté, from Latin plēnitātem, accusative of plēnitās (“fullness”), from plenus (“complete, full”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós (“full”), from which English full also comes, via Proto-Germanic. Related to the Latin derivatives replenish, plenary, complete, deplete, replete.

ex.en: There's still plenty that needs to be done.
ex.ja: やるべきことがまだたくさん残っている。

ex.en: Both Tom and Mary have plenty of personality.
ex.ja: トムもメアリーも個性豊かです。

ex.en: I have plenty of time to do that.
ex.ja: 私はそれをやるための多くの時間がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 plenus（満ちた）から。plen（満たす）+ ty。満ちていること →「たくさん」。complete（完全な）も同じ ple。

en: Someone who is preeminent in their field; a great person.
The (male) ruler or head of a principality.

prince.ety:
From Middle English prince, from Anglo-Norman prince, from Latin prī̆nceps (“first, foremost (person)”), from prīmus (“first”) + capiō (“seize, take”). Cognate with Old English fruma (“prince, ruler”). Doublet of princeps and principe.
Displaced English atheling (“prince”), from Middle English, from Old English æþeling (“prince”). Displaced also Middle English kinebarn (from cynebearn, literally “kinbairn”, i.e. “royal child”), alder < ealdor (“elder, leader, chief, prince, king”), and drighten < dryhten (“lord”).

ex.en: The prince learned English from the American lady.
ex.ja: 皇太子はそのアメリカ婦人から英語を習った。

ex.en: Prince Charles will be the next king of England.
ex.ja: チャールズ王子は次のイギリスの国王になるでしょう。

ex.en: The prince became a king that day.
ex.ja: 王子はその日、王になった。

Following the established standards of behavior or manners; correct or decorous.
Properly; thoroughly; completely.
A part of the Christian liturgy that varies according to the date.

ex.ja: その子は病院で適切な医療を受ける必要がある。

ex.en: He is the proper person for the job.
ex.ja: その仕事には彼が適任だ。

A measure of capacity used chiefly for grain or coal, varying greatly in quantity by time and location.
Pertaining to an aspect of a quarter.
Consisting of a fourth part, a quarter (¹⁄₄, 25%).
To divide into quarters; to divide by four.
To provide housing for (usually military personnel or equipment).

quarter.ety: From Middle English quarter, from Anglo-Norman quarter, from Latin quartarius, from quartus. Compare Spanish cuarto (“room, quarters; quarter”). Doublet of quartier.

ex.en: It's a quarter after nine in the morning.
ex.ja: 今は朝の９時１５分だよ。

ex.ja: 売り上げが４分の３に落ちた。

ex.ja: ケーキは４分の１食べたんだ。

en: Of, or pertaining to, a specific region or district.
Of, or pertaining to, a large geographic region.
An entity or event with scope limited to a single region.

regional.ety: From Middle French régional, from Latin regiōnālis, equivalent to region + -al.

ex.ja: この地方の名物料理がありますか。

ex.ja: インドは地域色豊かな食文化があります。

note.ja: region（地域）+ -al。ラテン語 regio（境界・地方）、regere（治める）。region と同じ。

en: A period of time devoted to a particular activity.
An official meeting or term of a council, court, or other body to conduct its business; e.g. the annual or semiannual periods of a legisl…
To hold or participate in a jam session with other musicians.

session.ety: From Middle English session, from Old French session, from Latin sessiō (“a sitting”), from sedeō (“sit”).

ex.ja: 彼等は貿易問題について臨時の会合を開いた。

ex.ja: 研修会は午後4時開始予定です。

With a descriptive word: the part of the sky which can be seen from a specific place or at a specific time; its climate, condition, etc.
To drink (a beverage) from a container without one's lips touching the container.
To clear (a high jump bar, hurdle, etc.) by a large margin.
